title: Writing the 1931 book: stock inserts and the choir on Wrap Your Troubles in Dreams
summary: He supplied some arrangements and inserts into stocks; the band's choir singing was done ad hoc and he felt it sounded poor with no backing from Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you write all of the book for the '31 band?
For the '31 -- some of the things that I wrote and some of them I would make just what you would call inserts -- insert parts, scripts inside.
Into the stock arrangement?
Into the stocks, yes.
Well, did the band ever make up any head arrangements?
One was on the singing.
The choir background?
Yeah, background. One was on the singing, because I wanted -- I had -- now, wait a minute. Now, that's this band now I'm talking about.
The first band.
The first band. Now, the other band, they sang what I wrote.
'Wrap Your Troubles In Dreams' was by the first band.
Yeah, 'Wrap Your Troubles in Dreams' -- I had the music -- I had the music going because I think at the time I had heard those choirs singing so beautifully and I had
made the arrangement for the band.

Well, Louie's first record of Basin Street Blues, which was made with -- when Earl Hines and Zutty and he were recording together -- small band -- Earl and Zutty and one other guy sang behind Louie as he scatted Basin -- you know -- that was about '28 I guess.
Uh-huh.
So, I guess he liked that sort of thing.

Well, yeah. He did. That was before my time. But now, about this, this is another thing we had that we didn't get -- we had a hang-up on -- the boys did not want to put their minds to getting this score down -- this vocal score. See, because I was right at the piano and I could give each one their parts, but they didn't want to do that. They just wanted to go -ba-da-ba-da-ba-da-- and all singing on the [ ] and everything. Well, that wasn't so hard. And I went along with the program. I had to go along with the program because I didn't get any backing up. I didn't get no backing up from that.
From Louie?
No, he didn't back up --
Well, he wasn't much of a disciplinarian.
Yeah, I didn't get no backing up for that. And when we were singing that thing, I was standing there, (unintelligible)
because it sounded terrible. It really sounded terrible. Yeah.
Well, you -- all the things that the '31 band recorded, you can get credit as arranging.
Yeah, they --
Is that correct?
They give me credit as arranging. I didn't make all, every, every one of them. Because if I had why they would have been playing a little more structure.
